q: The efficiencies of the steps of the energy chain of a power plant are $\eta_1 = 0.90$, $\eta_2 = 0.50$ and $\eta_3 = 0.96$. What is the efficiency of the whole chain?
a: The efficiencies are multiplied: $\eta = \eta_1 \eta_2 \eta_3 = 0.90 \cdot 0.50 \cdot 0.96 = 0.432 \approx 43\,\%$. They are not added or averaged.

q: The fuel power of a combined heat and power plant is $100\,\text{MW}$, the electric power $30\,\text{MW}$ and the district heating power $55\,\text{MW}$. What is the overall efficiency and how large is the power of waste heat?
a: $\eta_\text{tot} = (30\,\text{MW} + 55\,\text{MW})/100\,\text{MW} = 0.85 = 85\,\%$. The power of waste heat is $100\,\text{MW} - 85\,\text{MW} = 15\,\text{MW}$.

q: The efficiency of a hydropower plant is about 90%, but that of a condensing power plant about 40%. Why is the difference so big?
a: A hydropower plant converts the kinetic energy of water directly into mechanical energy in the turbine, and it is not a heat engine. So it does not have to release heat to the colder surroundings. A condensing power plant is a heat engine, and a large part of the energy of the fuel always goes to its condenser.
